title: Platform on-device ASR engine adapter (iOS SFSpeechRecognizer / Android SpeechRecognizer via channels)
accept: PlatformAsrEngine implements the listening-contracts AsrEngine interface over a method/event channel: start(biasing context) forwards the expected words to the native side (iOS: SFSpeechRecognizer contextualStrings; Android: SpeechRecognizer biasing), stop tears down the native session; verified with mocked platform channels (TestDefaultBinaryMessenger) asserting outgoing payloads and decoding scripted incoming hypothesis payloads.

Channel codec maps native hypothesis payloads (partial/final word hypotheses, confidence, optional phone-level detail where the platform exposes it) into the contract Hypothesis type; malformed payloads are dropped with a reported error, never crash the stream (negative tests).
Engine failure surfaces through the contract's failure signal so the tracker's tap fallback engages (mocked channel error test).
No audio buffers cross the channel to Dart and nothing is written to storage — the channel carries hypothesis metadata only (codec test asserts payload shape has no audio field).
[DEVICE] Native Swift/Kotlin recognition sessions, mic permission handling, and real hypothesis quality are owner-verified on physical devices; cannot compile or run in this container.

[BLOCKED-ON-OWNER] This ticket may only be built after the Unit 0 spike verdict exists in-repo and says keep-on-device (or specifies the alternative); the ticket's implementation cites the verdict per Unit 0 acceptance.
pinned_design: A-10 pinned: default ASR engine behind the hybrid matching layer = platform on-device recognition with contextual biasing (iOS SFSpeechRecognizer contextualStrings; Android SpeechRecognizer biasing), swappable behind Unit 4's engine interface if hypotheses prove too coarse. Unit 4 pinned: the adapter surfaces phone-level detail where the engine provides it; engine choice is invisible above the event-stream interface; no-retention processing mandatory. Unit 0 pinned: Unit 4's engine choice cites the spike verdict — the verdict gates this adapter (keep on-device / swap engine / hybrid).
notes: EXTERNAL BLOCKER: depends on the owner-delivered Unit 0 spike verdict (owner runs spike-asr-app on device with real children). Native side (Swift/Kotlin) is untestable in this container — written per platform API docs, marked for owner device testing; Dart side fully tested with mocked channels. This ticket owns AppDelegate.swift and MainActivity.kt (host-file registration) — no other ticket edits them; the spike's handlers register via documented snippets applied locally by the owner (see spike-asr-app notes). If the verdict says 'swap engine', this ticket is re-scoped by the orchestrator + owner before build.
